title: StreamSoccer: Event-Driven Memory for Streaming Soccer Commentary
abstract: arXiv:2608.19723v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Streaming video understanding requires models to causally update state as video arrives and organize growing history into semantic units that can evolve, persist, and be recalled under bounded computation and memory. This challenge is pronounced in live soccer commentary, where a system must describe completed events, summarize recent play, recall earlier events, or remain silent using only information available before each utterance. We present StreamSoccer, an event-driven system that uses event memory as its intermediate representation. A fixed-budget active memory integrates the stream; completed event states are retained locally and consolidated into retrievable historical records. A unified generator uses current, recent, and historical context to produce three commentary modes, while a rule-assisted scheduler selects a mode or silence. translated_title: StreamSoccer：面向流式足球解说的事件驱动记忆系统
translated_abstract: 流式视频理解要求模型在视频到达时因果地更新状态，并将不断增长的历史组织成语义单元，这些单元可以在有限的计算和记忆条件下演化、持久化并被召回。这一挑战在实时足球解说中尤为突出，系统必须描述已发生的事件、总结近期比赛、回忆更早的事件，或在每个话语之前仅使用可用信息保持沉默。我们提出了StreamSoccer，一个事件驱动系统，使用事件记忆作为其中间表示。一个固定预算的活跃记忆整合流式数据；完成的事件状态被本地保留并整合成可检索的历史记录。一个统一的生成器利用当前、近期和历史上下文产生三种解说模式，而一个规则辅助调度器选择一种模式或保持沉默。与围绕帧、视觉标记或缓存组织的流式视频语言模型不同，该系统强调事件语义，实现了高效的实时解说。
tldr: StreamSoccer通过事件驱动记忆和固定预算的活跃记忆机制，在流式足球解说中实现了对已完成事件、近期比赛和历史事件的动态处理与多模式解说生成。
en_tdlr: StreamSoccer uses event-driven memory with a fixed-budget active memory mechanism to dynamically process completed events, recent play, and historical records, enabling multi-mode commentary generation in streaming soccer.
